crossRefs.note: Jesus said these things, then lifting up his eyes to heaven, he said, “Father, the time has come. Glorify your Son…
Jesus, knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he came from God, and was going to God,
looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross…
He who has the bride is the bridegroom; but the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly…
I have spoken these things to you, that my joy may remain in you, and that your joy may be made full.
Therefore you now have sorrow, but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one will take your joy…
I have told you these things, that in me you may have peace. In the world you have trouble; but cheer up! I have…
Then he said to them, “Go your way. Eat the fat, drink the sweet, and send portions to him for whom nothing is…
Then I will go to the altar of God, to God, my exceeding joy. I will praise you on the harp, God, my God.
Those who sow in tears will reap in joy.
The disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.
for God’s Kingdom is not eating and drinking, but righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith,
And we write these things to you, that our joy may be fulfilled.
Having many things to write to you, I don’t want to do so with paper and ink, but I hope to come to you, and to speak…

translations.web: But now I come to you, and I say these things in the world, that they may have my joy made full in themselves.
translations.bsb: But now I am coming to You; and I am saying these things while I am in the world, so that they may have My joy fulfilled within them.
translations.kjv: And now come I to thee; and these things I speak in the world, that they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves.
translations.asv: But now I come to thee; and these things I speak in the world, that they may have my joy made full in themselves.
